status: experimental threat model; not a finding catalog
core_invariant: Reusable institutional patterns may carry structure and evidence obligations, but must never carry ambient runtime authority into a local deployment.

attack_classes.risk: Imported pattern encodes installation, role, credential, vote, or package provenance as permission.
Authority follows a person after term expiry, removal, or role change.
Qualification or membership credential is treated as execution authority.
Recognition by one institution silently creates trust or authority in another.
A reusable package is applied outside its legal/policy scope.
Pattern embeds subdelegation or privilege expansion.
Vote or threshold result becomes direct execution authority.
Recovery or acting-office mechanism restores stale/revoked authority.
Pattern omits review/remedy for consequential institutional decisions.
Reusable identifiers create unnecessary cross-domain surveillance.
Malicious or substituted reusable package changes policy semantics.
Same primitive label means different authority semantics across adapters.

nonclaims: A reusable pattern is not law, policy, accreditation, certification, or authority.
A valid package is not safe for every jurisdiction or institution.
An institutional decision record does not prove arbitrary external-world truth.
This model does not authorize live public-sector, clinical, financial, criminal-justice, election, or other high-coercion deployment.
